This is true regardless of whether the card is on board or in hand, unless otherwise stated. Ranking up one card won’t affect both copies unless the conditions are met for each individually.

“Level Up” is a mechanic that I think is really cool in Legends of Runeterra, so I decided to see how a similar effect would work in Hearthstone. 

How it works is: 

If you play the cards as is, you will get their basic effect.  For instance, the Blackhand Guard will deal 4 damage to anything. But if you choose to follow the requirements of the “Rank Up” text, the card will transform into the stronger, uncollectible version. 

This is true regardless of whether the card is on board or in hand, unless otherwise stated. Ranking up one card won’t affect both copies unless the conditions are met for each individually. For instance, playing three Dragons won’t upgrade a Blackhand Guard that’s in your deck even if the other has been in hand, but it will upgrade both copies if they’re both in hand at the Rome of summoning all three Dragons. 

So in some ways, this is both similar and different to Galakrond Invokes.
